thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need a deterministic fallback order for route selectors that match multiple aliases with different compatibility constraints. Example: route A accepts alias:billing-fast (v1,q8) and alias:billing-safe (v2,fp16,strict). Which should we prefer?
alex: My vote: prefer strict compatibility (billing-safe) if the client's headers indicate strict=true, otherwise prefer lower-latency (billing-fast). But we need a global tie-breaker.
cheng: +1. Also propose a policy level: route policy -> per-tenant overrides -> header hints -> tag weights -> last-resort model. So deterministic but pluggable.
maria: Proposed tie-breaker order: 1) explicit model pin via header x-redwood-model-pin 2) route pin 3) tenant pin 4) compatibility score 5) cost/latency score 6) final fallback. Thoughts?
sam: Sounds reasonable. One caveat: compatibility score must penalize dequantized->quantized mismatches heavily. Otherwise quality regressions occur.
ui-liz: UX ask: Console should show which rule won and why (human readable). Also show telemetry: how often fallback happened and token cost delta. Can we add a "why" modal?
maria: Yes — add a "decision trace" field to route eval telemetry. Sample record: ```trace: ["header pin: none", "route pins: none", "compatibility: billing-safe score 0.9", "latency score: 0.6", "selected: billing-safe@v2"]``` That should be surfaced.
telemetry-bot: dev-telemetry: New event schema PR opened: route.decide.trace (fields: request_id, route_id, trace_steps, selected_model_alias). Link: https://git.redwood/schemas/PR-451
alex: Implementation detail: to keep eval cheap we should stop evaluating cost/latency when compatibility > 0.95 and header not set. Short-circuiting is fine.
cheng: Also need to consider quotas: if tenant is close to reserved capacity, routing should prefer cheaper quantized models even if lower compatibility, but only when auto-fallback allowed. Add quota threshold param in policy.
maria: Agreed. Let's add policy flag "allow_cost_based_fallback": true/false and quota_threshold_pct.
sam: Can we default allow_cost_based_fallback=false for enterprise customers?
maria: Yes and console default should be false for enterprise, true for self-serve.
ui-liz: UX: expose a toggle and an explanation tooltip: "When enabled, we'll choose a cheaper compatible model to avoid hitting reserved capacity; may affect output fidelity."
deploy-bot: deploy to staging started for route-service @eng-platform. CI 98% green.
maria: Cool — I'll write up a short design doc and add sample DSL for the console. Assigning action items: @alex implement selector priority, @cheng add quota hook, @ui-liz mock the "why" modal. Deadline EOD Friday.
alex: on it.
cheng: on it.
ui-liz: mock by Thurs noon.
